Read more -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Meloxicam (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meloxicam) citeturn293search8 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 9 months ago; Según Horacio Croxatto (del Instituto Chileno de Medicina Reproductiva (ICMeR), si nuevos estudios corroboran estos hallazgos, podría reemplazar a otros anticonceptivos de emergencia (como el acetato de ulipristal, la mifepristona y el levonorgestrel). El meloxicam es un AINE (antiinflamatorio no esteroideo, inhibidor de la ciclooxigenasa 2, COX2) utilizado habitualmente como analgésico, antiinflamatorio y antipirético -en procesos artríticos-, de fácil acceso y reducido precio, ha demostrado (estudios de 2009 y 2010) que inhibe la ovulación (impide la rotura del folículo que contiene el óvulo, por lo que este no podría ser fecundado), tomado en dosis de 30 mg durante cinco días seguidos después de la relación sexual se comporta como un eficaz anticonceptivo de urgencia. El meloxicam no altera el sistema endocrino y no causa alteraciones menstruales. Uno de los estudios ha sido llevado a cabo por Cristián Jesam, Ana María Salvatierra, Jill L. Schwartz y Horacio B. Croxatto, investigadores del Instituto Chileno de Medicina Reproductiva (ICMeR) y de la Facultad de Química y Biología, de la Universidad de Santiago de Chile. ## Marcas de comercialización Los nombres comerciales con los que se comercializa el meloxicam en Europa son, entre otros: * Tenaron * Aliviodol * Melox * Meloxicam * Mobec * Movalis * Recoba Los nombres comerciales con los que se comercializa el meloxicam en España son, entre otros: * Anaxicam * Ecax * Ilacox * Mavicam * Melocam * Mobic * Mobicox * Tenaron Algunas de las formulaciones veterinarias son:^{[cita requerida]} * Maxicam (Reco) * Meloxidyl * Metacam * Moxen * Petcam * Meloxivet ## Véase también * Piroxicam ## Enlaces externos * «Meloxicam», ficha en el sitio web Medline Plus. El meloxicam también se usa en la rama veterinaria. Productos de meloxicam se han fabricado y utilizado para diferentes especies del reino animal, con su principal aplicación en perros y gatos, pero también en bovinos, cerdos, caballos y cobayas.También se ha investigado como una alternativa al diclofenaco por la Real Sociedad para la Protección de las Aves (RSPB) para prevenir las muertes de buitres. Dependiendo de la especie, cada país o unión de países aplica diferentes directrices o marcos legales para el uso del medicamento, así como diferentes efectos secundarios registrados. Algunos de los efectos secundarios por el uso de meloxicam en animales, mencionados en la Agencia Europea de Medicamentos (EMA), son similares a los de los humanos, como irritación intestinal (vómitos, náusea y ulceración) y más improbables son efectos de toxicidad hepática y renal. ### El uso de Meloxicam en gatos -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Meloxicam for Dogs (https://www.thesprucepets.com/meloxicam-for-dogs-5197194) citeturn293news9 [wordlim: 100] Published: 5.1 years ago; Meloxicam is a prescription nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) commonly used in dogs to relieve pain and inflammation from osteoarthritis, injuries, or surgery. As a selective COX-2 inhibitor, it may cause fewer gastrointestinal effects than nonselective NSAIDs, though risks remain. Veterinary formulations are usually flavored liquid suspensions in 0.5 or 1.5 mg/mL strengths; human tablets may be dangerously concentrated and should never be given without veterinary instructions. The typical dose is once daily at 0.1 mg/kg, with an initial dose sometimes doubled at the veterinarian’s discretion. It may be given directly or with food, which can reduce stomach upset. Potential adverse effects include vomiting, diarrhea, gastrointestinal ulcers or bleeding, liver or kidney damage, and abnormal bleeding. Stop treatment and contact a veterinarian if side effects occur, and seek immediate care for severe lethargy, collapse, or profuse bleeding. Veterinary evaluation and laboratory testing are recommended before treatment, while long-term users generally need blood tests every three to six months. Meloxicam must not be combined with other NSAIDs or steroids unless specifically directed, and a washout period may be required. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Meloxicam (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meloxicam) citeturn293search10 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 4 months ago; Meloxicam ist ein Arzneistoff, genauer ein nichtsteroidales Antirheumatikum (NSAR, NSAID) aus der Gruppe der Oxicame. (https://www.verywellhealth.com/is-meloxicam-a-narcotic-8399786) citeturn293news16 [wordlim: 100] Published: 2.9 years ago; Meloxicam is not a narcotic or opioid. It is a prescription nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to reduce pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. Healthcare providers may also prescribe it off-label for other inflammatory conditions, including back pain. Unlike opioids, meloxicam is not considered addictive and does not cause opioid dependence or opioid use disorder. It is available in several formulations, with approved uses varying by form. Despite its benefits, meloxicam carries significant safety risks, including an increased risk of heart attack, stroke, stomach ulcers, and gastrointestinal bleeding, particularly with long-term use. Older adults and people with a history of ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding face greater risks. Meloxicam can also interact with other medications, including blood thinners, certain blood pressure drugs, and diuretics, potentially increasing bleeding or kidney problems. Patients should discuss their medical history, existing medications, and possible side effects with a healthcare provider before taking it. The maximum recommended adult dose is 15 mg once daily, and treatment should generally use the lowest effective dose for the shortest necessary duration. Nondrug approaches and alternative treatments may also help manage arthritis symptoms. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Meloxicam vs. Ibuprofen: What's the Difference? (https://www.verywellhealth.com/mobic-vs-ibuprofen-5118105) citeturn293news17 [wordlim: 100] Published: 5.6 years ago; Meloxicam and ibuprofen are nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) used to relieve pain and inflammation from conditions such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, bursitis, and tendinitis. Both work by blocking COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, reducing prostaglandins that cause pain, fever, and inflammation; however, this mechanism can also damage stomach protection and cause ulcers or bleeding. Meloxicam is prescription-only, generally stronger, and commonly dosed at 7.5 mg daily for chronic arthritis, while ibuprofen is available over the counter and is typically used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration. Despite meloxicam’s greater strength, studies suggest similar pain relief between the two drugs for back pain, with no clear efficacy advantage among NSAIDs. Both carry FDA black-box warnings for increased heart attack and stroke risk, as well as potentially serious gastrointestinal, kidney, and liver complications. They should not be taken together unless specifically directed by a healthcare professional.
